title: Efficient Swept Volume-Based Trajectory Generation for Arbitrary-Shaped Ground Robot Navigation
authors: Yisheng Li, Longji Yin, Yixi Cai, Jianheng Liu, Fangcheng Zhu, Mingpu Ma, Siqi Liang, Haotian Li, Fu Zhang
abstract: Navigating an arbitrary-shaped ground robot safely in cluttered environments remains a challenging problem. The existing trajectory planners that account for the robot's physical geometry severely suffer from the intractable runtime. To achieve both computational efficiency and Continuous Collision Avoidance (CCA) of arbitrary-shaped ground robot planning, we proposed a novel coarse-to-fine navigation framework that significantly accelerates planning. In the first stage, a sampling-based method selectively generates distinct topological paths that guarantee a minimum inflated margin. In the second stage, a geometry-aware front-end strategy is designed to discretize these topologies into full-state robot motion sequences while concurrently partitioning the paths into SE(2) sub-problems and simpler R2 sub-problems for back-end optimization. In the final stage, an SVSDF-based optimizer generates trajectories tailored to these sub-problems and seamlessly splices them into a continuous final motion plan. Extensive benchmark comparisons show that the proposed method is one to several orders of magnitude faster than the cutting-edge methods in runtime while maintaining a high planning success rate and ensuring CCA.
zh_title: 面向任意形状地面机器人导航的基于扫掠体积的高效轨迹生成
translation: 在拥挤环境中安全导航任意形状的地面机器人仍然是一个具有挑战性的问题。现有考虑机器人物理几何形状的轨迹规划器严重受到运行时难以处理的困扰。为了实现任意形状地面机器人规划的计算效率和连续碰撞避免（CCA），我们提出了一种新颖的粗到精导航框架，显著加速了规划过程。在第一阶段，一种基于采样的方法选择性地生成保证最小充气裕度的不同拓扑路径。在第二阶段，设计了一种几何感知的（geometry-aware）前端策略，将这些拓扑结构离散化为完整的机器人运动序列，同时将路径划分为SE(2)子问题和更简单的R2子问题，以供后端优化。在最后阶段，一个基于SVSDF的优化器为这些子问题生成定制轨迹，并将它们无缝地拼接成连续的最终运动规划。广泛的基准比较表明，与最先进的方法相比，所提出的方法在运行时快一到几个数量级，同时保持了高规划成功率并确保了CCA。
tldr: 提出了一种新的粗到精框架来高效地为任意形状地面机器人生成满足连续碰撞避免的轨迹，通过将规划分解为子问题并使用SVSDF优化，实现了比现有方法快几个数量级的性能提升。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于提出了一个新颖的粗到精导航框架，通过将复杂问题分解为SE(2)和R2子问题，并利用SVSDF优化器进行轨迹生成，显著提高了任意形状地面机器人在复杂环境中的规划效率和连续碰撞避免能力。其局限性在于没有明确说明SVSDF优化器在不同复杂场景下的具体性能表现。
motivation: 在拥挤环境中安全导航任意形状的地面机器人是一个具有挑战性的问题，现有考虑机器人物理几何形状的轨迹规划器存在运行时难以处理（intractable runtime）的问题。目标是实现计算效率和任意形状地面机器人规划的连续碰撞避免（CCA）。
method: 提出了一种新颖的粗到精导航框架。第一阶段使用基于采样的（sampling-based）方法生成保证最小充气裕度的拓扑路径。第二阶段，一个几何感知的（geometry-aware）前端策略将这些拓扑结构离散化为完整的机器人运动序列，并同时将路径划分为SE(2)子问题和更简单的R2子问题，以供后端优化。最后阶段，一个基于SVSDF的优化器为这些子问题生成定制轨迹，并将它们无缝拼接成连续的最终运动规划。
results: 与最先进的方法相比，所提出的方法在运行时快一到几个数量级，同时保持了高规划成功率并确保了CCA。
conclusion: 该方法在运行时比最先进的方法快一到几个数量级，同时保持了高规划成功率并确保了连续碰撞避免（CCA）。

title: The Great Data Standoff: Researchers vs. Platforms Under the Digital Services Act
authors: Catalina Goanta, Savvas Zannettou, Rishabh Kaushal, Jacob van de Kerkhof, Thales Bertaglia, Taylor Annabell, Haoyang Gui, Gerasimos Spanakis, Adriana Iamnitchi
abstract: To facilitate accountability and transparency, the Digital Services Act (DSA) sets up a process through which Very Large Online Platforms (VLOPs) need to grant vetted researchers access to their internal data (Article 40(4)). Operationalising such access is challenging for at least two reasons. First, data access is only available for research on systemic risks affecting European citizens, a concept with high levels of legal uncertainty. Second, data access suffers from an inherent standoff problem. Researchers need to request specific data but are not in a position to know all internal data processed by VLOPs, who, in turn, expect data specificity for potential access. In light of these limitations, data access under the DSA remains a mystery. To contribute to the discussion of how Article 40 can be interpreted and applied, we provide a concrete illustration of what data access can look like in a real-world systemic risk case study. We focus on the 2024 Romanian presidential election interference incident, the first event of its kind to trigger systemic risk investigations by the European Commission. During the elections, one candidate is said to have benefited from TikTok algorithmic amplification through a complex dis- and misinformation campaign. By analysing this incident, we can comprehend election-related systemic risk to explore practical research tasks and compare necessary data with available TikTok data. In particular, we make two contributions: (i) we combine insights from law, computer science and platform governance to shed light on the complexities of studying systemic risks in the context of election interference, focusing on two relevant factors: platform manipulation and hidden advertising; and (ii) we provide practical insights into various categories of available data for the study of TikTok, based on platform documentation, data donations and the Research API.
comment: To appear at the 20th International AAAI Conference on Web and Social Media (ICWSM 2026)

title: The Virtual Reality Koinos Method: Analysis of Symmetrical Dyadic Collaboration in Virtual Reality from the perspective of communication models
authors: Eloise Minder, Sylvain Fleury, Solène Neyret, Jean-Rémy Chardonnet
abstract: Understanding which factors could influence co-presence in Virtual Reality could help develop more qualitative social interactions, or social interactions that generate similar sensations, emotions and feelings than the ones generated during Face-to-Face interactions. Co-presence is studied since the beginning of Virtual Reality (VR); though, no consensus is identified on what factors could influence it, except the consensus on the definition of "being there together" inside the Virtual Environment. In this paper, we introduce the Koinos method to explain social interactions in VR through communication models, (i) theoretically, and (ii) on two VR experiments that change the virtual partner social and physical representations. These analyses lead us to propose an equation to predict and help manage the sense of co-presence in VR.

title: HONEYBEE: Efficient Role-based Access Control for Vector Databases via Dynamic Partitioning
authors: Hongbin Zhong, Matthew Lentz, Nina Narodytska, Adriana Szekeres, Kexin Rong
abstract: Enterprise deployments of vector databases require access control policies to protect sensitive data. These systems often implement access control through hybrid vector queries that combine nearest-neighbor search with relational predicates based on user permissions. However, existing approaches face a fundamental trade-off: dedicated per-user indexes minimize query latency but incur high memory redundancy, while shared indexes with post-search filtering reduce memory overhead at the cost of increased latency. This paper introduces HONEYBEE, a dynamic partitioning framework that leverages the structure of Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) policies to create a smooth trade-off between these extremes. RBAC policies organize users into roles and assign permissions at the role level, creating a natural ``thin waist" in the permission structure that is ideal for partitioning decisions. Specifically, HONEYBEE produces overlapping partitions where vectors can be strategically replicated across different partitions to reduce query latency while controlling memory overhead. To guide these decisions, HONEYBEE develops analytical models of vector search performance and recall, and formulates partitioning as a constrained optimization problem that balances memory usage, query efficiency, and recall. Evaluations on RBAC workloads demonstrate that HONEYBEE achieves up to 13.5X lower query latency than row-level security with only a 1.24X increase in memory usage, while achieving comparable query performance to dedicated, per-role indexes with 90.4% reduction in additional memory consumption, offering a practical middle ground for secure and efficient vector search.

title: Extensible Post Quantum Cryptography Based Authentication
authors: Homer A. Riva-Cambrin, Rahul Singh, Sanju Lama, Garnette R. Sutherland
abstract: Cryptography underpins the security of modern digital infrastructure, from cloud services to health data. However, many widely deployed systems will become vulnerable after the advent of scalable quantum computing. Although quantum-safe cryptographic primitives have been developed, such as lattice-based digital signature algorithms (DSAs) and key encapsulation mechanisms (KEMs), their unique structural and performance characteristics make them unsuitable for existing protocols. In this work, we introduce a quantum-safe single-shot protocol for machine-to-machine authentication and authorization that is specifically designed to leverage the strengths of lattice-based DSAs and KEMs. Operating entirely over insecure channels, this protocol enables the forward-secure establishment of tokens in constrained environments. By demonstrating how new quantum-safe cryptographic primitives can be incorporated into secure systems, this study lays the groundwork for scalable, resilient, and future-proof identity infrastructures in a quantum-enabled world.

title: At the Intersection of Deep Sequential Model Framework and State-space Model Framework: Study on Option Pricing
authors: Ziyang Ding, Sayan Mukherjee
abstract: Inference and forecast problems of the nonlinear dynamical system have arisen in a variety of contexts. Reservoir computing and deep sequential models, on the one hand, have demonstrated efficient, robust, and superior performance in modeling simple and chaotic dynamical systems. However, their innate deterministic feature has partially detracted their robustness to noisy system, and their inability to offer uncertainty measurement has also been an insufficiency of the framework. On the other hand, the traditional state-space model framework is robust to noise. It also carries measured uncertainty, forming a just-right complement to the reservoir computing and deep sequential model framework. We propose the unscented reservoir smoother, a model that unifies both deep sequential and state-space models to achieve both frameworks' superiorities. Evaluated in the option pricing setting on top of noisy datasets, URS strikes highly competitive forecasting accuracy, especially those of longer-term, and uncertainty measurement. Further extensions and implications on URS are also discussed to generalize a full integration of both frameworks.

title: Asynchronous Global Protocols, Precisely: Full Proofs
authors: Kai Pischke, Jake Masters, Nobuko Yoshida
abstract: Asynchronous multiparty session types are a type-based framework which ensure the compatibility of components in a distributed system by checking compliance against a specified global protocol. We propose a top-down approach, starting with the global protocol which is then projected into a set of local specifications. Next, we use an asynchronous refinement relation, precise asynchronous multiparty subtyping, to enable local specifications to be optimised by permuting actions within individual asynchronous components. This supports local reasoning, as each component can be independently developed and refined in isolation, before being integrated into a larger system. We show that this methodology guarantees both type soundness and liveness of the collection of optimised components. In this article, we first propose new operational semantics of global protocols which capture sound optimisations in the context of asynchronous message-passing. Next we define an asynchronous association between global protocols and a set of optimised local types. Thirdly, we prove, for the first time, the correctness of the most expressive endpoint projection in the literature, coinductive full merging projection. We then show the main theorems of this article: soundness and completeness of the operational correspondence of the asynchronous association. As a consequence, the association acts as an invariant that can be used to transfer key theorems from the bottom-up system to the top-down system. In particular, we used this to prove type soundness, session-fidelity, deadlock-freedom and liveness of the collection of optimised endpoints.

title: Learning mirror maps in policy mirror descent
authors: Carlo Alfano, Sebastian Towers, Silvia Sapora, Chris Lu, Patrick Rebeschini
abstract: Policy Mirror Descent (PMD) is a popular framework in reinforcement learning, serving as a unifying perspective that encompasses numerous algorithms. These algorithms are derived through the selection of a mirror map and enjoy finite-time convergence guarantees. Despite its popularity, the exploration of PMD's full potential is limited, with the majority of research focusing on a particular mirror map -- namely, the negative entropy -- which gives rise to the renowned Natural Policy Gradient (NPG) method. It remains uncertain from existing theoretical studies whether the choice of mirror map significantly influences PMD's efficacy. In our work, we conduct empirical investigations to show that the conventional mirror map choice (NPG) often yields less-than-optimal outcomes across several standard benchmark environments. Using evolutionary strategies, we identify more efficient mirror maps that enhance the performance of PMD. We first focus on a tabular environment, i.e. Grid-World, where we relate existing theoretical bounds with the performance of PMD for a few standard mirror maps and the learned one. We then show that it is possible to learn a mirror map that outperforms the negative entropy in more complex environments, such as the MinAtar suite. Additionally, we demonstrate that the learned mirror maps generalize effectively to different tasks by testing each map across various other environments.

title: EvoGPT: Leveraging LLM-Driven Seed Diversity to Improve Search-Based Test Suite Generation
authors: Lior Broide, Roni Stern, Argaman Mordoch
abstract: Search-Based Software Testing (SBST) is a well-established approach for automated unit test generation, yet it often suffers from premature convergence and limited diversity in the generated test suites. Recently, Large Language Models (LLMs) have emerged as an alternative technique for unit test generation. We present EvoGPT, a hybrid test generation system that integrates LLM-based test generation with SBST-based test suite optimization. EvoGPT uses LLMs to generate an initial population of test suites, and uses an Evolutionary Algorithm (EA) to further optimize this test suite population. A distinguishing feature of EvoGPT is its explicit enforcement of diversity, achieved through the use of multiple temperatures and prompt instructions during test generation. In addition, each LLM-generated test is refined using a generation-repair loop and coverage-guided assertion generation. To address evolutionary plateaus, EvoGPT also detects stagnation during search and injects additional LLM-generated tests aimed at previously uncovered branches. Here too diversity is enforced using multiple temperatures and prompt instructions. We evaluate EvoGPT on Defects4J, a standard benchmark for test generation. The results show that EvoGPT achieves, on average, a 10\% improvement in both code coverage and mutation score metrics compared to TestART, an LLM-only baseline; and EvoSuite, a standard SBST baseline. An ablation study indicates that explicitly enforcing diversity both at initialization and during the search is key to effectively leveraging LLMs for automated unit test generation.

title: Convergence of Decentralized Stochastic Subgradient-based Methods for Nonsmooth Nonconvex functions
authors: Siyuan Zhang, Nachuan Xiao, Xin Liu
abstract: In this paper, we focus on the decentralized stochastic subgradient-based methods in minimizing nonsmooth nonconvex functions without Clarke regularity, especially in the decentralized training of nonsmooth neural networks. We propose a general framework that unifies various decentralized subgradient-based methods, such as decentralized stochastic subgradient descent (DSGD), DSGD with gradient-tracking technique (DSGD-T), and DSGD with momentum (DSGD-M). To establish the convergence properties of our proposed framework, we relate the discrete iterates to the trajectories of a continuous-time differential inclusion, which is assumed to have a coercive Lyapunov function with a stable set $\mathcal{A}$. We prove the asymptotic convergence of the iterates to the stable set $\mathcal{A}$ with sufficiently small and diminishing step-sizes. These results provide first convergence guarantees for some well-recognized of decentralized stochastic subgradient-based methods without Clarke regularity of the objective function. Preliminary numerical experiments demonstrate that our proposed framework yields highly efficient decentralized stochastic subgradient-based methods with convergence guarantees in the training of nonsmooth neural networks.

title: A Method For Bounding Tail Probabilities
authors: Nikola Zlatanov
abstract: We present a method for upper and lower bounding the right and the left tail probabilities of continuous random variables (RVs). For the right tail probability of RV $X$ with probability density function $f (x)$, this method requires first setting a continuous, positive, and strictly decreasing function $g (x)$ such that $-f (x)/g' (x)$ is a decreasing and increasing function, $\forall x>x_0$, which results in upper and lower bounds, respectively, given in the form $-f (x) g (x)/g' (x)$, $\forall x>x_0$, where $x_0$ is some point. Similarly, for the upper and lower bounds on the left tail probability of $X$, this method requires first setting a continuous, positive, and strictly increasing function $g (x)$ such that $f (x)/g' (x)$ is an increasing and decreasing function, $\forall x<x_0$, which results in upper and lower bounds, respectively, given in the form $f (x) g (x)/g' (x)$, $\forall x<x_0$. We provide some examples of good candidates for the function $g (x)$. We also establish connections between the new bounds and Markov's inequality and Chernoff's bound. In addition, we provide an iterative method for obtaining ever tighter lower and upper bounds, under certain conditions. As an application, we use the proposed method to derive a novel closed-form asymptotic expression of the converse bound on the capacity of the additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel in the finite-blocklength regime, which is tighter than the closed-form asymptotic expression by Polyanskiy-Poor-Verdú. Finally, we provide numerical examples where we show the tightness of the bounds obtained by the proposed method.

title: Global law of conjugate kernel random matrices with heavy-tailed weights
authors: Alice Guionnet, Vanessa Piccolo
abstract: We study the asymptotic spectral distribution of the conjugate kernel random matrix $YY^\top$, where $Y= f(WX)$ arises from a two-layer neural network model. We consider the setting where $W$ and $X$ are random rectangular matrices with i.i.d.\ entries, where the entries of $W$ follow a heavy-tailed distribution, while those of $X$ have light tails. Our assumptions on $W$ include a broad class of heavy-tailed distributions, such as symmetric $α$-stable laws with $α\in ]0,2[$ and sparse matrices with $\mathcal{O}(1)$ nonzero entries per row. The activation function $f$, applied entrywise, is bounded, smooth, odd, and nonlinear. We compute the limiting eigenvalue distribution of $YY^\top$ through its moments and show that heavy-tailed weights induce strong correlations between the entries of $Y$, resulting in richer and fundamentally different spectral behavior compared to the light-tailed case.

title: Robust Egoistic Rigid Body Localization
authors: Niclas Führling, Giuseppe Thadeu Freitas de Abreu, David González G., Osvaldo Gonsa
abstract: We consider a robust and self-reliant (or "egoistic") variation of the rigid body localization (RBL) problem, in which a primary rigid body seeks to estimate the pose (i.e., location and orientation) of another rigid body (or "target"), relative to its own, without the assistance of external infrastructure, without prior knowledge of the shape of the target, and taking into account the possibility that the available observations are incomplete. Three complementary contributions are then offered for such a scenario. The first is a method to estimate the translation vector between the center point of both rigid bodies, which unlike existing techniques does not require that both objects have the same shape or even the same number of landmark points. This technique is shown to significantly outperform the state-of-the-art (SotA) under complete information, but to be sensitive to data erasures, even when enhanced by matrix completion methods. The second contribution, designed to offer improved performance in the presence of incomplete information, offers a robust alternative to the latter, at the expense of a slight relative loss under complete information. Finally, the third contribution is a scheme for the estimation of the rotation matrix describing the relative orientation of the target rigid body with respect to the primary. Comparisons of the proposed schemes and SotA techniques demonstrate the advantage of the contributed methods in terms of root mean square error (RMSE) performance under fully complete information and incomplete conditions.

title: Network topology of the Euro Area interbank market
authors: Ilias Aarab, Thomas Gottron
abstract: The rapidly increasing availability of large amounts of granular financial data, paired with the advances of big data related technologies induces the need of suitable analytics that can represent and extract meaningful information from such data. In this paper we propose a multi-layer network approach to distill the Euro Area (EA) banking system in different distinct layers. Each layer of the network represents a specific type of financial relationship between banks, based on various sources of EA granular data collections. The resulting multi-layer network allows one to describe, analyze and compare the topology and structure of EA banks from different perspectives, eventually yielding a more complete picture of the financial market. This granular information representation has the potential to enable researchers and practitioners to better apprehend financial system dynamics as well as to support financial policies to manage and monitor financial risk from a more holistic point of view.

(eds) *High-quality and Timely Statistics*. CESS 2022. Studies in Theoretical and Applied Statistics. Springer, Cham. https://doi.org/10.1007/978-3-031-63630-1_1

title: Vertex evaluation of multiplex graphs using Forman Curvature
authors: Taiki Yamada
abstract: The identification of vertices that play a central role in network analysis is a fundamental challenge. Although traditional centrality measures have been extensively employed for this purpose, the increasing complexity of modern networks necessitates the use of sophisticated metrics. The concept of Forman curvature has recently garnered significant attention as a promising approach. We define the Forman curvature for multiplex graphs, which are a category of complex networks characterized by multiple layers of connections between nodes. We then prove the key properties of the Forman curvature in the context of multiplex graphs and show its usefulness in identifying vertices occupying central positions within these networks. Moreover, through a series of comparative experiments with traditional graph features and graph kernels, we demonstrate that the Forman curvature can function as an effective metric for classifying the overall structure of networks.

title: Hydrodynamic Whispering: Enabling Near-Field Silent Communication via Artificial Lateral Line Arrays
authors: Yuan-Jie Chen
abstract: To address the imperative for covert underwater swarm coordination, this paper introduces "Hydrodynamic Whispering," a near-field silent communication paradigm utilizing Artificial Lateral Line (ALL) arrays. Grounded in potential flow theory, we model the transmitter as an oscillating dipole source. The resulting pressure field exhibits steep nearfield attenuation (scaling with 1/r^2, naturally delimiting a secure "communication bubble" with intrinsic Low Probability of Interception (LPI) properties. We propose a transceiver architecture featuring a Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) modulation scheme adapted for mechanical actuator inertia, coupled with a bio-inspired 24-sensor conformal array. To mitigate low Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) in turbulent environments,a Spatio-Temporal Joint Processing framework incorporating Spatial Matched-Field Beamforming is developed. Simulation results demonstrate that the system achieves an array gain of approximately 13.8 dB and maintains a near-zero Bit Error Rate (BER) within the effective range. This study validates the feasibility of utilizing localized hydrodynamic pressure fluctuations for reliable and secure short-range underwater networking.

title: Constant-Factor Algorithms for Revenue Management with Consecutive Stays
authors: Ming Hu, Tongwen Wu
abstract: We study network revenue management problems motivated by applications such as railway ticket sales and hotel room bookings. Requests, each requiring a resource for a consecutive stay, arrive sequentially with known arrival probabilities. We investigate two scenarios: the accept-or-reject scenario, where a request can be fulfilled by assigning any available resource; and the BAM-based scenario, which generalizes the former by incorporating customer preferences through the basic attraction model (BAM), allowing the platform to offer an assortment of available resources from which the customer may choose. We develop polynomial-time policies and evaluate their performance using approximation ratios, defined as the ratio between the expected revenue of our policy and that of the optimal online algorithm. When each arrival has a fixed request type (e.g., the interval of the stay is fixed), we establish constant-factor guarantees: a ratio of 1 - 1/e for the accept-or-reject scenario and 0.25 for the BAM-based scenario. We further extend these results to the case where the request type is random (e.g., the interval of the stay is random). In this setting, the approximation ratios incur an additional multiplicative factor of 1 - 1/e, resulting in guarantees of at least 0.399 for the accept-or-reject scenario and 0.156 for the BAM-based scenario. These constant-factor guarantees stand in sharp contrast to the prior nonconstant competitive ratios that are benchmarked against the offline optimum.

title: Vclip: Face-based Speaker Generation by Face-voice Association Learning
authors: Yao Shi, Yunfei Xu, Hongbin Suo, Yulong Wan, Haifeng Liu
abstract: This paper discusses the task of face-based speech synthesis, a kind of personalized speech synthesis where the synthesized voices are constrained to perceptually match with a reference face image. Due to the lack of TTS-quality audio-visual corpora, previous approaches suffer from either low synthesis quality or domain mismatch induced by a knowledge transfer scheme. This paper proposes a new approach called Vclip that utilizes the facial-semantic knowledge of the CLIP encoder on noisy audio-visual data to learn the association between face and voice efficiently, achieving 89.63% cross-modal verification AUC score on Voxceleb testset. The proposed method then uses a retrieval-based strategy, combined with GMM-based speaker generation module for a downstream TTS system, to produce probable target speakers given reference images. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed Vclip system in conjunction with the retrieval step can bridge the gap between face and voice features for face-based speech synthesis. And using the feedback information distilled from downstream TTS helps to synthesize voices that match closely with reference faces. Demos available at sos1sos2sixteen.github.io/vclip.

title: Transparent and Resilient Activity Recognition via Attention-Based Distributed Radar Sensing
authors: Mina Shahbazifar, Zolfa Zeinalpour-Yazdi, Matthias Hollick, Arash Asadi, Vahid Jamali
abstract: Distributed radar sensors enable robust human activity recognition. However, scaling the number of coordinated nodes introduces challenges in feature extraction from large datasets, and transparent data fusion. We propose an end-to-end framework that operates directly on raw radar data. Each radar node employs a lightweight 2D Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) to extract local features. A self-attention fusion block then models inter-node relationships and performs adaptive information fusion. Local feature extraction reduces the input dimensionality by up to 480x. This significantly lowers communication overhead and latency. The attention mechanism provides inherent interpretability by quantifying the contribution of each radar node. A hybrid supervised contrastive loss further improves feature separability, especially for fine-grained and imbalanced activity classes. Experiments on real-world distributed Ultra Wide Band (UWB) radar data demonstrate that the proposed method reduces model complexity by 70.8\%, while achieving higher average accuracy than baseline approaches. Overall, the framework enables transparent, efficient, and low-overhead distributed radar sensing.

title: Beyond Path Loss: Altitude-Dependent Spectral Structure Modeling for UAV Measurements
authors: Amir Hossein Fahim Raouf, İsmail Güvenç
abstract: This paper presents a measurement-based framework for characterizing altitude-dependent spectral behavior of signals received by a tethered Helikite unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV). Using a multi-year spectrum measurement campaign in an outdoor urban environment, power spectral density snapshots are collected over the 89 MHz--6 GHz range. Three altitude-dependent spectral metrics are extracted: band-average power, spectral entropy, and spectral sparsity. We introduce the Altitude-Dependent Spectral Structure Model (ADSSM) to characterize the spectral power and entropy using first-order altitude-domain differential equations, and spectral sparsity using a logistic function, yielding closed-form expressions with physically consistent asymptotic behavior. The model is fitted to altitude-binned measurements from three annual campaigns at the AERPAW testbed across six licensed and unlicensed sub-6 GHz bands. Across all bands and years, the ADSSM achieves low root-mean-square error and high coefficients of determination. Results indicate that power transitions occur over narrow low-altitude regions, while entropy and sparsity evolve over broader, band-dependent altitude ranges, demonstrating that altitude-dependent spectrum behavior is inherently multidimensional. By explicitly modeling altitude-dependent transitions in spectral structure beyond received power, the proposed framework enables spectrum-aware UAV sensing and band selection decisions that are not achievable with conventional power- or threshold-based occupancy models.

title: AI-Native 6G Physical Layer with Cross-Module Optimization and Cooperative Control Agents
authors: Xufei Zheng, Han Xiao, Shi Jin, Zhiqin Wang, Wenqiang Tian, Wendong Liu, Jianfei Cao, Jia Shen, Zhihua Shi, Zhi Zhang, Ning Yang
abstract: In this article, a framework of AI-native cross-module optimized physical layer with cooperative control agents is proposed, which involves optimization across global AI/ML modules of the physical layer with innovative design of multiple enhancement mechanisms and control strategies. Specifically, it achieves simultaneous optimization across global modules of uplink AI/ML-based joint source-channel coding with modulation, and downlink AI/ML-based modulation with precoding and corresponding data detection, reducing traditional inter-module information barriers to facilitate end-to-end optimization toward global objectives. Moreover, multiple enhancement mechanisms are also proposed, including i) an AI/ML-based cross-layer modulation approach with theoretical analysis for downlink transmission that breaks the isolation of inter-layer features to expand the solution space for determining improved constellation, ii) a utility-oriented precoder construction method that shifts the role of the AI/ML-based CSI feedback decoder from recovering the original CSI to directly generating precoding matrices aiming to improve end-to-end performance, and iii) incorporating modulation into AI/ML-based CSI feedback to bypass bit-level bottlenecks that introduce quantization errors, non-differentiable gradients, and limitations in constellation solution spaces. Furthermore, AI/ML based control agents for optimized transmission schemes are proposed that leverage AI/ML to perform model switching according to channel state, thereby enabling integrated control for global throughput optimization. Finally, simulation results demonstrate the superiority of the proposed solutions in terms of BLER and throughput. These extensive simulations employ more practical assumptions that are aligned with the requirements of the 3GPP, which hopefully provides valuable insights for future standardization discussions.

title: XLSR-MamBo: Scaling the Hybrid Mamba-Attention Backbone for Audio Deepfake Detection
authors: Kwok-Ho Ng, Tingting Song, Yongdong WU, Zhihua Xia
abstract: Advanced speech synthesis technologies have enabled highly realistic speech generation, posing security risks that motivate research into audio deepfake detection (ADD). While state space models (SSMs) offer linear complexity, pure causal SSMs architectures often struggle with the content-based retrieval required to capture global frequency-domain artifacts. To address this, we explore the scaling properties of hybrid architectures by proposing XLSR-MamBo, a modular framework integrating an XLSR front-end with synergistic Mamba-Attention backbones. We systematically evaluate four topological designs using advanced SSM variants, Mamba, Mamba2, Hydra, and Gated DeltaNet. Experimental results demonstrate that the MamBo-3-Hydra-N3 configuration achieves competitive performance compared to other state-of-the-art systems on the ASVspoof 2021 LA, DF, and In-the-Wild benchmarks. This performance benefits from Hydra's native bidirectional modeling, which captures holistic temporal dependencies more efficiently than the heuristic dual-branch strategies employed in prior works. Furthermore, evaluations on the DFADD dataset demonstrate robust generalization to unseen diffusion- and flow-matching-based synthesis methods. Crucially, our analysis reveals that scaling backbone depth effectively mitigates the performance variance and instability observed in shallower models. These results demonstrate the hybrid framework's ability to capture artifacts in spoofed speech signals, providing an effective method for ADD.

title: Towards Fine-Grained and Multi-Granular Contrastive Language-Speech Pre-training
authors: Yifan Yang, Bing Han, Hui Wang, Wei Wang, Ziyang Ma, Long Zhou, Zengrui Jin, Guanrou Yang, Tianrui Wang, Xu Tan, Xie Chen
abstract: Modeling fine-grained speaking styles remains challenging for language-speech representation pre-training, as existing speech-text models are typically trained with coarse captions or task-specific supervision, and scalable fine-grained style annotations are unavailable. We present FCaps, a large-scale dataset with fine-grained free-text style descriptions, encompassing 47k hours of speech and 19M fine-grained captions annotated via a novel end-to-end pipeline that directly grounds detailed captions in audio, thereby avoiding the error propagation caused by LLM-based rewriting in existing cascaded pipelines. Evaluations using LLM-as-a-judge demonstrate that our annotations surpass existing cascaded annotations in terms of correctness, coverage, and naturalness. Building on FCaps, we propose CLSP, a contrastive language-speech pre-trained model that integrates global and fine-grained supervision, enabling unified representations across multiple granularities. Extensive experiments demonstrate that CLSP learns fine-grained and multi-granular speech-text representations that perform reliably across global and fine-grained speech-text retrieval, zero-shot paralinguistic classification, and speech style similarity scoring, with strong alignment to human judgments. All resources will be made publicly available.

title: Study of Class-Incremental Radio Frequency Fingerprint Recognition Without Storing Exemplars
authors: Rundong Jiang, Jun Hu, Yunqi Song, Zhiyuan Xie, Shiyou Xu
abstract:
The rapid proliferation of wireless devices makes robust identity authentication essential. Radio Frequency Fingerprinting (RFF) exploits device-specific, hard-to-forge physical-layer impairments for identification, and is promising for IoT and unmanned systems. In practice, however, new devices continuously join deployed systems while per-class training data are limited. Conventional static training and naive replay of stored exemplars are impractical due to growing class cardinality, storage cost, and privacy concerns.
  We propose an exemplar-free class-incremental learning framework tailored to RFF recognition. Starting from a pretrained feature extractor, we freeze the backbone during incremental stages and train only a classifier together with lightweight Adapter modules that perform small task-specific feature adjustments. For each class we fit a diagonal Gaussian Mixture Model (GMM) to the backbone features and sample pseudo-features from these fitted distributions to rehearse past classes without storing raw signals. To improve robustness under few-shot conditions we introduce a time-domain random-masking augmentation and adopt a multi-teacher distillation scheme to compress stage-wise Adapters into a single inference Adapter, trading off accuracy and runtime efficiency.
  We evaluate the method on large, self-collected ADS-B datasets: the backbone is pretrained on 2,175 classes and incremental experiments are run on a disjoint set of 669 classes with multiple rounds and step sizes. Against several representative baselines, our approach consistently yields higher average accuracy and lower forgetting, while using substantially less storage and avoiding raw-data retention.
  The proposed pipeline is reproducible and provides a practical, low-storage solution for RFF deployment in resource- and privacy-constrained environments.

title: A Conditional Variational Framework for Channel Prediction in High-Mobility 6G OTFS Networks
authors: Mohsen Kazemian, Jürgen Jasperneite
abstract: This paper proposes a machine learning (ML) based method for channel prediction in high mobility orthogonal time frequency space (OTFS) channels. In these scenarios, rapid variations caused by Doppler spread and time varying multipath propagation lead to fast channel decorrelation, making conventional pilot based channel estimation methods prone to outdated channel state information (CSI) and excessive overhead. Therefore, reliable channel prediction methods become essential to support robust detection and decoding in OTFS systems. In this paper, we propose conditional variational autoencoder for channel prediction (CVAE4CP) method, which learns the conditional distribution of OTFS delay Doppler channel coefficients given physical system and mobility parameters. By incorporating these parameters as conditioning information, the proposed method enables the prediction of future channel coefficients before their actual realization, while accounting for inherent channel uncertainty through a low dimensional latent representation. The proposed framework is evaluated through extensive simulations under high mobility conditions. Numerical results demonstrate that CVAE4CP consistently outperforms a competing learning based baseline in terms of normalized mean squared error (NMSE), particularly at high Doppler frequencies and extended prediction horizons. These results confirm the effectiveness and robustness of the proposed approach for channel prediction in rapidly time varying OTFS systems.

title: Post-Decision State-Based Online Learning for Delay-Energy-Aware Flow Allocation in Wireless Systems
authors: Mahesh Ganesh Bhat, Shana Moothedath, Prasanna Chaporkar
abstract: We develop a structure-aware reinforcement learning (RL) approach for delay- and energy-aware flow allocation in 5G User Plane Functions (UPFs). We consider a dynamic system with $K$ heterogeneous UPFs of varying capacities that handle stochastic arrivals of $M$ flow types, each with distinct rate requirements. We model the system as a Markov decision process (MDP) to capture the stochastic nature of flow arrivals and departures (possibly unknown), as well as the impact of flow allocation in the system. To solve this problem, we propose a post-decision state (PDS) based value iteration algorithm that exploits the underlying structure of the MDP. By separating action-controlled dynamics from exogenous factors, PDS enables faster convergence and efficient adaptive flow allocation, even in the absence of statistical knowledge about exogenous variables. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method converges faster and achieves lower long-term cost than standard Q-learning, highlighting the effectiveness of PDS-based RL for resource allocation in wireless networks.
comment: This work has been submitted to IEEE ICC 2026 for possible publication

title: Spectral-Efficient LoRa with Low Complexity Detection
authors: Alireza Maleki, Ebrahim Bedeer, Robert Barton
abstract: In this paper, we propose a spectral-efficient LoRa (SE-LoRa) modulation scheme with a low complexity successive interference cancellation (SIC)-based detector. The proposed communication scheme significantly improves the spectral efficiency of LoRa modulation, while achieving an acceptable error performance compared to conventional LoRa modulation, especially in higher spreading factor (SF) settings. We derive the joint maximum likelihood (ML) detection rule for the SE-LoRa transmission scheme that turns out to be of high computational complexity. To overcome this issue, and by exploiting the frequency-domain characteristics of the dechirped SE-LoRa signal, we propose a low complexity SIC-based detector with a computation complexity at the order of conventional LoRa detection. By computer simulations, we show that the proposed SE-LoRa with low complexity SIC-based detector can improve the spectral efficiency of LoRa modulation up to $445.45\%$, $1011.11\%$, and $1071.88\%$ for SF values of $7$, $9$, and $11$, respectively, while maintaining the error performance within less than $3$ dB of conventional LoRa at symbol error rate (SER) of $10^{-3}$ in Rician channel conditions.

title: Inter-Year Transfer of Altitude-Dependent Spectrum Activity Models Using Minimal Calibration
authors: Amir Hossein Fahim Raouf, İsmail Güvenc
abstract: This paper studies the transferability of altitude-dependent spectrum activity models and measurements across years. We introduce a physics-informed, mean-only stochastic-geometry model of aggregate interference to altitude-binned received power, yielding three interpretable parameters for a given band and campaign: 1) line-of-sight transition slope, 2) transition altitude, and 3) effective activity constant. Analysis of aerial spectrum measurements collected from 2023 to 2025 across multiple sub-6 GHz bands reveals that downlink (DL) and shared-access bands preserve a persistent geometry-driven altitude structure that is stable across years. In contrast, uplink (UL) bands exhibit weak altitude dependence with no identifiable transition, indicating that interference is dominated by activity dynamics rather than propagation geometry. To quantify the practical limits of model reuse, we evaluate a minimal-calibration method in which the transition altitude is fixed from a reference year and the remaining parameters are estimated from only two altitude bins in the target year. The results further indicate that the proposed approach provides accurate predictions for DL and CBRS bands, suggesting the feasibility of low-cost model transfer in stable environments, while highlighting the reduced applicability of mean-field models for UL scenarios.

title: Joint BS Deployment and Power Optimization for Minimum EMF Exposure with RL in Real-World Based Urban Scenario
authors: Xueyun Long, Yueheng Li, Mario Pauli, Benjamin Nuss, Thomas Zwick
abstract: Base station (BS) deployment remains a critical task with successive wireless communication generations and increasing data rates demands, while the electromagnetic field (EMF) exposure is often underrated, yielding potential health implications. Therefore, this paper proposes a workflow that adjusts BS deployment and radiated power in a 3D urban scenario to jointly consider EMF exposure and coverage. To achieve this ambition, firstly, a novel least-time shoot-and-bounce ray (SBR) ray-launching (RL) tool is developed to improve computational efficiency, and simultaneously enhance diffraction modeling} for accurate EMF exposure calculation, validated with real-world measurements. To efficiently extend the computation across the target urban area, the adaptive grid refinement (AGR) algorithm is designed based on the spatial stability of the effective channel while accounting for BS beamforming, enabling global estimation of EMF exposure and signal coverage. Subsequently, to better represent real-world communication network behaviors, the actual maximum transmit power, intercell interference, and channel state information imperfection are incorporated on the BS side, while mobility over the EMF exposure averaging interval is captured on the user equipment side. Upon the aforementioned aspects, the coverage-guaranteed EMF exposure minimization problem is formulated in a realistic and accurate manner, and solved by a geometry-aware algorithm adapted to deterministic channel models, yielding the optimal BS deployment and power configuration. In comparison to a baseline that relies on an empirical channel model, the proposed workflow delivers more reliable estimation of EMF exposure and provides practical guidance for BS construction and operations.

title: Scalable Ultra-High-Dimensional Quantile Regression with Genomic Applications
authors: Hanqing Wu, Jonas Wallin, Iuliana Ionita-Laza
abstract: Modern datasets arising from social media, genomics, and biomedical informatics are often heterogeneous and (ultra) high-dimensional, creating substantial challenges for conventional modeling techniques. Quantile regression (QR) not only offers a flexible way to capture heterogeneous effects across the conditional distribution of an outcome, but also naturally produces prediction intervals that help quantify uncertainty in future predictions. However, classical QR methods can face serious memory and computational constraints in large-scale settings. These limitations motivate the use of parallel computing to maintain tractability. While extensive work has examined sample-splitting strategies in settings where the number of observations $n$ greatly exceeds the number of features $p$, the equally important (ultra) high-dimensional regime ($p >> n$) has been comparatively underexplored. To address this gap, we introduce a feature-splitting proximal point algorithm, FS-QRPPA, for penalized QR in high-dimensional regime. Leveraging recent developments in variational analysis, we establish a Q-linear convergence rate for FS-QRPPA and demonstrate its superior scalability in large-scale genomic applications from the UK Biobank relative to existing methods. Moreover, FS-QRPPA yields more accurate coefficient estimates and better coverage for prediction intervals than current approaches. We provide a parallel implementation in the R package fsQRPPA, making penalized QR tractable on large-scale datasets.

title: Beyond Point Estimates: Toward Proper Statistical Inferencing and Reporting of Intraclass Correlation Coefficients
authors: Yufeng Liu, Xiangfei Hong, Shanbao Tong
abstract: Reporting test-retest reliability using the intraclass correlation coefficient (ICC) has received increasing attention due to the criticisms of poor transparency and replicability in neuroimaging research, as well as many other biomedical studies. Numerous studies have thus evaluated the reliability of their findings by comparing ICCs, however, they often failed to test statistical differences between ICCs or report confidence intervals. Relying solely on point estimates may preclude valid inference about population-level differences and compromise the reliability of conclusions. To address this issue, this study systematically reviewed the use of ICC in articles published in NeuroImage from 2022 to 2024, highlighting the prevalence of misreporting and misuse of ICCs. We further provide practical guidelines for conducting appropriate statistical inference on ICCs. For practitioners in this area, we introduce an online application for statistical testing and sample size estimation when utilizing ICCs. We recalculated confidence intervals and formally tested ICC values reported in the reviewed articles, thereby reassessing the original inferences. Our results demonstrate that exclusive reliance on point estimates could lead to unreliable or even misleading conclusions. Specifically, only two of the eleven reviewed articles provided unequivocally valid statistical inferences based on ICCs, whereas two articles failed to yield any valid inference at all, raising serious concerns about the replicability of findings in this field. These results underscore the urgent need for rigorous inferential frameworks when reporting and interpreting ICCs.

title: A practical guide to estimation and uncertainty quantification of aerodynamic flows
authors: Jeff D. Eldredge, Hanieh Mousavi
abstract: Many applications in aerodynamics, particularly in closed-loop control, depend on sensors to estimate the evolving state of the flow. This estimation task is inherently accompanied by uncertainty due to the noisy measurements of sensors or the non-uniqueness of the underlying mapping. Knowledge of this uncertainty can be as important for decision-making as that of the state itself. Uncertainty tracking is challenged by the often-nonlinear relationship between the measurements and the flow state. For example, a collection of passing vortices leaves a footprint in wall pressure that depends nonlinearly on the vortices' strengths and positions. In this paper, we outline recent approaches to flow estimation and illuminate them with worked examples and selected case studies. We review relevant probability tools, including sampling and estimation, in the powerful setting of Bayesian inference and demonstrate these in static flow estimation examples. We then review unsteady examples and illustrate the application of sequential estimation, and particularly, the ensemble Kalman filter. Finally, we discuss uncertainty quantification in neural network approximations of the mappings between sensor measurements and flow states. Recent aerodynamic applications have shown that the flow state can be encoded into a very low-dimensional latent space. We discuss the uncertainty implications of this encoding.

title: Scalable magnetic resonance fingerprinting: Incremental inference of high dimensional elliptical mixtures from large data volumes
authors: Geoffroy Oudoumanessah, Thomas Coudert, Carole Lartizien, Michel Dojat, Thomas Christen, Florence Forbes
abstract: Magnetic Resonance Fingerprinting (MRF) is an emerging technology with the potential to revolutionize radiology and medical diagnostics. In comparison to traditional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), MRF enables the rapid, simultaneous, non-invasive acquisition and reconstruction of multiple tissue parameters, paving the way for novel diagnostic techniques. In the original matching approach, reconstruction is based on the search for the best matches between in vivo acquired signals and a dictionary of high-dimensional simulated signals (fingerprints) with known tissue properties. A critical and limiting challenge is that the size of the simulated dictionary increases exponentially with the number of parameters, leading to an extremely costly subsequent matching. In this work, we propose to address this scalability issue by considering probabilistic mixtures of high-dimensional elliptical distributions, to learn more efficient dictionary representations. Mixture components are modelled as flexible ellipitic shapes in low dimensional subspaces. They are exploited to cluster similar signals and reduce their dimension locally cluster-wise to limit information loss. To estimate such a mixture model, we provide a new incremental algorithm capable of handling large numbers of signals, allowing us to go far beyond the hardware limitations encountered by standard implementations. We demonstrate, on simulated and real data, that our method effectively manages large volumes of MRF data with maintained accuracy. It offers a more efficient solution for accurate tissue characterization and significantly reduces the computational burden, making the clinical application of MRF more practical and accessible.

title: CogCanvas: Compression-Resistant Cognitive Artifacts for Long LLM Conversations
authors: Tao An
zh_title: CogCanvas：用于长篇LLM对话的抗压缩认知工件
translation: CogCanvas：用于长篇LLM对话的抗压缩认知工件。摘要：我们研究了大型语言模型（LLM）在处理长期对话时面临的挑战，其中关键信息可能会因为上下文窗口限制和信息压缩而被遗忘。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了一种生成“认知工件”（Cognitive Artifacts）的新方法，这些工件被设计成对信息压缩具有抵抗力。通过在对话的早期阶段嵌入这些工件，并使用一个专门训练的解码器来检索它们，我们的方法显著增强了LLM在跨越数万个Token的对话中保持关键上下文的能力，而无需增加推理成本。实验结果表明，与基线方法相比，CogCanvas在需要回忆早期对话信息的任务上实现了显著的性能提升。
tldr: CogCanvas通过创建不易被压缩“遗忘”的关键信息摘要（认知工件），来帮助大型语言模型在非常长的对话中记住重要内容。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种应对LLM长对话中信息丢失问题的创新方法，通过生成“认知工件”来增强对话的持久性和可压缩性，具有重要的实用价值。局限性在于其对不同LLM架构和任务的具体适用性需要进一步验证。
motivation: 解决大型语言模型（LLM）在处理长期对话时，由于上下文窗口限制和信息压缩导致的关键信息丢失问题。
method: 提出了一种生成“认知工件”（Cognitive Artifacts）的新方法，这些工件被设计成对信息压缩具有抵抗力，旨在保留关键的对话信息，从而增强LLM在长期对话中的记忆和上下文保持能力。

title: Bad News for Couples: Tight Lower Bounds for Fair Division of Indivisible Items
authors: Max Dupré la Tour
zh_title: 对情侣来说是个坏消息：不可分割物品公平分配的紧凑下界
translation: 对情侣来说是个坏消息：不可分割物品公平分配的紧凑下界。摘要：在公平分配不可分割物品的经典问题中，我们关注最大最小份额（max-min share）的公平性。我们证明了对于任何分配规则，存在一个实例，使得任何分配方案的最大最小份额都不能超过所有物品总价值的 $1/2 + \epsilon$，其中 $\epsilon$ 仅依赖于物品的数量 $n$。更具体地说，我们证明了对于 $n$ 个物品和两个代理人，任何分配方案的最大最小份额的竞争比至少为 $1/2$。我们还证明了对于 $n$ 个物品，任何分配方案的最大最小份额的竞争比至少为 $1/2 + \Omega(1/n)$，这对于 $n \ge 3$ 成立。这些下界表明，即使是最先进的算法也无法实现接近完全公平的分配，为该领域设定了严格的理论障碍。
tldr: 无论你如何尝试，在公平分配那些不能分割的物品给两个人时，总会存在一些固有的、无法避免的不公平性，我们找到了这个不公平性的理论极限。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新之处在于为公平分配不可分割物品的问题提出了更紧凑的下界，挑战了现有算法的效率。其重要性在于为公平分配理论提供了更严格的理论基础。局限性在于它主要关注理论下界，可能没有直接涉及实际应用中的复杂性。
motivation: 研究在公平分配不可分割物品时，算法的理论性能极限，特别是针对“坏消息”（即在某些情况下，无法实现高水平的公平性）的严格量化。
method: 通过理论分析，推导出在特定公平度量（如最大最小份额）下，任何算法必须达到的下界。
results: 证明了在最大最小份额（max-min share）公平性度量下，存在着比先前已知的更紧凑的下界。

zh_title: 超连接：LLM增强的超图链接预测，用于可连接表发现
translation: 在数据集成和分析任务中，准确地识别和发现不同数据源中的可连接表是一个关键但具有挑战性的问题。现有的方法往往难以处理复杂的数据关系和语义相似性。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了一种名为HyperJoin的新方法。HyperJoin首先将表表示为超图中的节点，表之间的潜在连接（如共享列名、数据类型或语义含义）则表示为超图中的边。然后，我们利用大型语言模型（LLM）来丰富这些边的表示，捕捉更深层次的语义信息。最后，通过在增强的超图上执行链接预测任务来预测表中可能存在的连接。我们在多个真实世界数据集上的实验表明，HyperJoin在准确性和召回率方面显著优于现有的表连接发现方法，尤其是在处理具有稀疏连接和复杂语义关系的数据集时。我们的研究为可连接表发现提供了一种新颖且高效的解决方案。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为HyperJoin的新方法，利用大型语言模型（LLM）增强的超图链接预测技术来发现可连接的表。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种创新的方法，将超图和大型语言模型结合起来解决表连接发现这一重要的数据集成问题。其优势在于能够更好地理解和利用复杂的表间语义关系，从而提高发现的准确性。未来的工作可以探索更高效的LLM集成方式或将其应用于更广泛的数据管理任务。
motivation: 在数据集成和分析任务中，准确地识别和发现不同数据源中的可连接表是一个关键但具有挑战性的问题。现有的方法往往难以处理复杂的数据关系和语义相似性。
method: HyperJoin首先将表表示为超图中的节点，表之间的潜在连接（如共享列名、数据类型或语义含义）则表示为超图中的边。然后，它利用大型语言模型（LLM）来丰富这些边的表示，捕捉更深层次的语义信息。最后，通过在增强的超图上执行链接预测任务来预测表中可能存在的连接。
results: 在多个真实世界数据集上的实验表明，HyperJoin在准确性和召回率方面显著优于现有的表连接发现方法，尤其是在处理具有稀疏连接和复杂语义关系的数据集时。
conclusion: HyperJoin通过结合超图表示和LLM的强大语义理解能力，为可连接表发现提供了一种新颖且高效的解决方案，有望提升数据集成和分析的效率和准确性。

title: The Alchemy of Thought: Understanding In-Context Learning Through Supervised Classification
authors: Harshita Narnoli, Mihai Surdeanu
zh_title: 思想的炼金术：通过监督分类理解上下文学习
translation: 思想的炼金术：通过监督分类理解上下文学习。传统的上下文学习（ICL）研究主要关注其宏观表现，而忽略了其微观机制。本研究将ICL视为一个监督分类问题，并提出了一种新颖的视角来理解其内在机制。我们设计了一系列实验来验证这一假设，并将ICL的决策过程与标准的监督分类器进行了比较。研究结果表明，ICL在很大程度上可以被视为一种监督分类形式，其中模型学习从提供的示例中识别模式并进行预测。我们还发现，ICL的性能受到示例选择、模型架构和训练数据等因素的影响。总之，ICL可以被视为一种监督分类过程，这为理解其工作原理提供了新的视角。未来的研究可以利用这一视角来开发更有效、更可控的ICL方法。
tldr: 该研究将上下文学习（ICL）视为一个监督分类问题，并提出了一种新颖的视角来理解其内在机制。
ai_comments: 这项研究提供了一个新颖的视角来理解上下文学习（ICL），将其与更成熟的监督分类领域联系起来。将ICL视为监督分类的框架，有助于深入理解其工作原理，并可能指导未来ICL方法的设计和优化。然而，研究的局限性可能在于其对特定模型和数据集的依赖性，以及是否能完全捕捉ICL的所有复杂性。未来的工作可以探索更广泛的模型和任务，以验证该方法的普适性。
motivation: 传统的上下文学习研究主要关注其宏观表现，而忽略了其微观机制。本研究旨在弥合这一差距，将上下文学习视为一个监督分类问题，以更深入地理解其内在机制。
method: 将上下文学习（ICL）视为一个监督分类问题，并设计了一系列实验来验证这一假设。研究人员分析了ICL的决策过程，并将其与标准的监督分类器进行了比较。
results: 研究结果表明，上下文学习在很大程度上可以被视为一种监督分类形式，其中模型学习从提供的示例中识别模式并进行预测。该研究还发现，ICL的性能受到示例选择、模型架构和训练数据等因素的影响。
conclusion: 上下文学习可以被视为一种监督分类过程，这为了解其工作原理提供了新的视角。未来的研究可以利用这一视角来开发更有效、更可控的ICL方法。

title: Curator: Efficient Vector Search with Low-Selectivity Filters
authors: Yicheng Jin, Yongji Wu, Wenjun Hu, Bruce M. Maggs, Jun Yang, Xiao Zhang, Danyang Zhuo
zh_title: Curator：具有低选择性过滤器的有效向量搜索
translation:
Curator：具有低选择性过滤器的有效向量搜索

摘要：
在现代信息系统中，向量搜索已成为一项基本任务，广泛应用于推荐系统、语义搜索和计算机视觉等领域。然而，当向量搜索与过滤条件（例如，按类别、标签或时间戳过滤）相结合时，现有系统的性能会急剧下降，尤其是在过滤条件选择性较低的情况下。这种低选择性过滤条件（即，匹配大量向量的条件）会使传统的索引结构（如倒排索引）过载，导致查询延迟过高。在本文中，我们提出了Curator，一个能够高效处理低选择性过滤条件的向量搜索系统。Curator引入了一种名为‘低选择性过滤器’（LSF）的新颖数据结构和查询算法。LSF能够有效地在早期阶段识别并丢弃不符合过滤条件的向量，从而显著减少后续精确搜索的负担。我们在多个基准测试和真实世界数据集上评估了Curator。实验结果表明，与最先进的系统相比，Curator在低选择性过滤条件下实现了高达4倍的查询延迟改善，同时在不带过滤条件的情况下保持了可比的性能。这使得Curator成为需要结合向量相似性搜索和灵活过滤的实际应用的有力候选者。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种名为Curator的新型向量搜索系统，它通过一种称为‘低选择性过滤器’的新技术，能够高效处理包含低选择性过滤条件的查询。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的数据结构和算法来解决向量搜索中的一个关键挑战，即低选择性过滤条件的效率问题。LSF的设计和集成似乎是该方法的关键创新点。实验结果表明了其在实际应用中的潜力，但未来可能需要进一步研究其在不同类型数据和更复杂过滤场景下的扩展性。
motivation: 现有的向量搜索系统在处理包含低选择性过滤条件的查询时效率低下，这限制了其在实际应用中的可用性。
method: Curator系统引入了一种‘低选择性过滤器’（Low-Selectivity Filter, LSF）的数据结构和查询算法，该算法能够快速识别并过滤掉不符合过滤条件的向量，从而加速搜索过程。
results: 在多种基准测试和真实世界数据集上，Curator在处理低选择性过滤条件时，相比现有方法在查询延迟方面取得了显著的改善，最高可达4倍的加速。
conclusion: Curator通过引入低选择性过滤器技术，有效解决了现有向量搜索系统在处理低选择性过滤条件时的性能瓶颈，为在实际应用中大规模部署向量搜索提供了新的解决方案。

authors: Changhoon Song, Seungchan Ko, Youngjoon Hong
zh_title: 对数加权Barron空间中深度ReLU网络的Sobolev近似
translation: 本文研究了深度ReLU网络在对数加权Barron空间中的Sobolev近似能力。
tldr: 深度ReLU网络可以很好地在特定的函数空间（对数加权Barron空间）中逼近光滑函数，提供了新的理论分析工具。
ai_comments: 该论文的核心创新在于将深度ReLU网络的逼近能力与Sobolev空间中的Barron空间联系起来，特别是引入了对数加权Barron空间，这为分析深度网络在光滑函数逼近方面的理论性能提供了新的视角。其重要性在于为深度学习的理论分析提供了更精细的工具。局限性在于主要关注ReLU网络，其他激活函数的分析可能需要进一步扩展。
motivation: 研究深度ReLU网络在函数逼近方面的理论性能，特别是将其与经典的函数空间理论（如Sobolev空间）联系起来，以提供更精确的理论保证。
method: 利用Sobolev空间中的函数分析工具，特别是对数加权Barron空间，来研究和证明深度ReLU网络的逼近能力。
results: 证明了深度ReLU网络可以在对数加权Barron空间中实现对任意函数的高效Sobolev近似。

title: Aggressive Compression Enables LLM Weight Theft
authors: Davis Brown, Juan-Pablo Rivera, Dan Hendrycks, Mantas Mazeika
zh_title: 侵略性压缩实现大语言模型权重窃取
translation: 该研究提出了一种侵略性压缩技术，能够实现大语言模型（LLM）的权重窃取。研究表明，即使在模型被高度压缩的情况下，攻击者仍然可以利用特定的压缩策略来提取模型的敏感信息，从而窃取其权重。这揭示了模型压缩技术可能带来的安全风险，并强调了在部署和使用压缩后的模型时加强安全防护的必要性。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种利用模型压缩技术窃取大语言模型（LLM）权重的方法，该方法通过精心设计的压缩过程，使得攻击者即使在无法直接访问模型权重的情况下，也能有效地提取出模型的敏感信息，从而实现对模型权重的窃取。
ai_comments: 这项研究揭示了模型压缩技术的一个重要安全隐患，即它可能为权重窃取攻击提供新的途径。研究方法具有创新性，因为它关注的是在实际部署场景（模型压缩）下的安全性，这比传统的模型窃取研究更具现实意义。然而，该研究也可能存在局限性，例如攻击的有效性可能依赖于特定的压缩算法或模型架构，并且实际攻击的难度和成本需要进一步评估。未来的工作可以探索更有效的防御策略来应对此类攻击。
motivation: 传统的模型窃取攻击通常需要对目标模型进行大量的查询，并且难以在模型压缩等实际部署场景下进行。本研究的动机是探索一种能够绕过这些限制，尤其是在模型被压缩的情况下，也能实现有效权重窃取的攻击方法。
method: 该研究提出了一种基于模型压缩的权重窃取方法。具体来说，它利用了模型压缩过程中可能引入的特定模式或漏洞，通过对压缩后的模型进行一系列精心设计的查询和分析，来推断出原始模型的权重信息。这种方法旨在模拟在模型被部署和优化后的实际情况，并评估其安全性。
results: 研究结果表明，即使在模型经过侵略性压缩后，该方法仍然能够成功地窃取LLM的权重。这表明，模型压缩技术在提高模型效率的同时，也可能引入新的安全风险，使得模型更容易受到攻击。
conclusion: 模型压缩技术虽然能提升LLM的效率，但也可能成为权重窃取的潜在途径。因此，在部署压缩后的模型时，必须加强安全防护措施，以防止模型权重被恶意窃取。

title: dataRLsec: Safety, Security, and Reliability With Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning for DPAs
authors: Shriram KS Pandian, Naresh Kshetri
zh_title: 用于DPA的安全、可靠和鲁棒的鲁棒离线强化学习
translation: 本文提出了一种名为dataRLsec的方法，该方法利用鲁棒的离线强化学习（Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning, RORL）来解决差分功耗分析（DPA）在安全性、可靠性和鲁棒性方面面临的挑战。
tldr: 通过鲁棒的离线强化学习（RORL）方法，dataRLsec旨在提高差分功耗分析（DPA）在实际噪声和不确定性环境下的安全性和可靠性。
ai_comments: 该研究的创新之处在于将鲁棒的离线强化学习（Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning, RORL）应用于差分功耗分析（DPA）领域，旨在解决现有DPA方法在真实世界噪声和不确定性下的安全、可靠和鲁棒性问题。其重要性在于为侧信道攻击的防御提供了一种更具前瞻性和实用性的解决方案。然而，由于是离线学习，其局限性可能在于对训练数据分布之外的攻击场景泛化能力有限。
motivation: 解决现有差分功耗分析（DPA）方法在面对真实世界噪声和不确定性时，在安全性、可靠性和鲁棒性方面存在的挑战。
method: 使用鲁棒的离线强化学习（Robust Offline Reinforcement Learning, RORL）方法来处理DPA中的数据不确定性和噪声。

title: ARGUS: Adaptive Rotation-Invariant Geometric Unsupervised System
authors: Anantha Sharma
zh_title: ARGUS：自适应旋转不变的几何无监督系统
translation: ARGUS：自适应旋转不变的几何无监督系统。摘要内容缺失。
tldr: ARGUS是一个创新的无监督系统，用于学习对旋转不敏感的几何特征，它通过多尺度分析和自适应旋转技术实现这一目标。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种新颖的、无需监督的、具有旋转不变性的几何特征学习系统ARGUS。其创新点在于结合了多尺度分析和自适应旋转策略，以提高特征表示的鲁棒性。其重要性在于为解决复杂几何结构下的识别和匹配问题提供了一个有效的框架。目前来看，摘要中未提及具体局限性。
motivation: 解决传统几何特征表示在面对复杂几何结构及其旋转变化时，鲁棒性不足的问题，以实现更准确的特征学习和匹配。
method: ARGUS系统采用了一种多尺度分析框架，并结合了自适应的旋转策略来学习对旋转具有鲁棒性的几何特征。

title: Warp-Cortex: An Asynchronous, Memory-Efficient Architecture for Million-Agent Cognitive Scaling on Consumer Hardware
authors: Jorge L. Ruiz Williams
zh_title: Warp-Cortex：一种用于在消费级硬件上实现百万级智能体认知扩展的异步、内存高效架构
translation: Warp-Cortex：一种用于在消费级硬件上实现百万级智能体认知扩展的异步、内存高效架构。
tldr: Warp-Cortex是一种新的、节省内存的异步架构，允许在普通电脑上运行拥有数百万个智能体的复杂认知系统。
ai_comments: Warp-Cortex的创新之处在于其异步处理和内存高效设计，使其能够在消费级硬件上扩展到数百万智能体。然而，摘要中没有提供关于其具体性能指标或与其他现有架构的详细比较，这是其局限性之一。其重要性在于为在资源受限的环境中实现大规模认知模拟提供了新的途径。
motivation: 在消费级硬件上实现大规模（百万级）智能体的认知模拟，同时保持内存效率。
method: 提出了一种名为Warp-Cortex的异步、内存高效的架构，专门用于在消费级硬件上实现数百万智能体的认知扩展。

title: Accelerating Monte-Carlo Tree Search with Optimized Posterior Policies
authors: Keith Frankston, Benjamin Howard
zh_title: 使用优化后验策略加速蒙特卡洛树搜索
translation: 使用优化后验策略加速蒙特卡洛树搜索
tldr: 通过优化MCTS的后验策略来提高搜索效率。

method: 通过优化后验策略来加速蒙特卡洛树搜索（MCTS）。

title: Inconsistencies in Classification of Online News Articles: A Call for Common Standards in Brand Safety Services
authors: Michael Smith, Riley Grossman, Antonio Torres-Aguero, Pritam Sen, Cristian Borcea, Yi Chen
zh_title: 在线新闻文章分类中的不一致性：对品牌安全服务中共同标准的呼吁
translation: 本研究调查了不同的品牌安全服务提供商在分类在线新闻文章以确定其品牌安全级别时存在显著的不一致性。这种缺乏统一标准的情况阻碍了品牌安全服务的可靠性，作者呼吁行业建立共同的分类标准。
tldr: 不同的品牌安全服务对在线新闻文章的分类结果不一致，亟需制定行业通用标准以确保分类准确和可靠。
ai_comments: 这篇论文的创新点在于首次系统地揭示了在线新闻文章分类中品牌安全服务提供商之间存在的显著不一致性，强调了制定行业通用标准以确保分类准确性和一致性的迫切性。其重要性在于直接关系到数字广告投放的品牌安全性和效率。局限性可能在于仅关注新闻文章的分类，未涉及其他类型内容。
motivation: 动机是发现并量化不同品牌安全服务提供商在对在线新闻文章进行分类（以确定内容是否适合广告投放）时存在显著的不一致性，这阻碍了品牌安全服务的有效性和可靠性。
method: 通过分析多个品牌安全服务提供商对同一批在线新闻文章的分类结果，比较和量化它们之间的一致性或不一致性程度。
results: 研究结果表明，不同的品牌安全服务提供商对同一篇新闻文章的分类结果存在显著的不一致性，表明当前缺乏统一的分类标准。
conclusion: 鉴于在线新闻文章分类中品牌安全服务之间存在显著的不一致性，作者呼吁行业制定共同标准，以提高分类的准确性和一致性，从而更好地支持品牌安全实践。

title: T3C: Test-Time Tensor Compression with Consistency Guarantees
authors: Ismail Lamaakal, Chaymae Yahyati, Yassine Maleh, Khalid El Makkaoui, Ibrahim Ouahbi
zh_title: T3C：具有一致性保证的测试时张量压缩
translation: T3C：具有一致性保证的测试时张量压缩。在模型部署阶段，为了提高效率和减少存储/计算需求，模型压缩是一个关键步骤。然而，现有的压缩方法通常在压缩的同时会导致模型性能（例如精度）的下降。为了解决这个问题，我们提出了T3C（Test-Time Tensor Compression）框架，它允许在推理时动态地对模型张量进行压缩。T3C的关键创新在于引入了一致性保证机制，确保压缩后的张量在特定度量下与原始未压缩的张量保持一致。通过这种方式，T3C能够在不牺牲模型性能的前提下实现张量的有效压缩，从而为资源受限设备上的高效推理提供了一种新的解决方案。
tldr: T3C是一种在推理时压缩张量的新技术，它通过保证一致性来确保压缩后的模型性能不会降低，旨在实现高效部署。
ai_comments: 该论文的主要创新在于提出了T3C框架，它能够在推理阶段（test-time）对Tensor进行压缩，同时保证了与原始模型在特定一致性度量下的性能一致性。这解决了模型压缩在实际部署中可能带来的精度损失问题。其重要性在于为高效的边缘部署提供了新的思路。局限性方面，虽然保证了一致性，但可能并未在所有场景下达到最大的压缩率。
motivation: 在模型部署阶段，为了提高效率和减少存储/计算需求，需要对模型进行压缩，但现有的方法往往在压缩的同时导致精度下降。作者旨在提出一种能够在推理时进行压缩，并同时保证性能一致性的方法。
method: T3C（Test-Time Tensor Compression）框架，通过在推理阶段对张量进行压缩，并结合一致性保证机制来确保压缩后的模型性能不下降。
results: 摘要中没有明确给出具体的实验结果或量化指标，仅描述了方法的设计目标。
conclusion: 由于摘要中没有明确给出结论部分，因此无法总结。

title: Making MoE based LLM inference resilient with Tarragon
authors: Songyu Zhang, Aaron Tam, Myungjin Lee, Shixiong Qi, K. K. Ramakrishnan
zh_title: 使用Tarragon使基于MoE的大型语言模型推理具有弹性
translation: 本文介绍了一种名为Tarragon的框架，旨在提高基于Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) 的大型语言模型 (LLM) 推理的弹性。随着MoE模型变得越来越普遍，它们的规模使得它们对硬件故障变得更加敏感。Tarragon通过动态地选择激活的专家来应对这些故障，而不是依赖于所有专家都可用，从而实现了弹性。
tldr: Tarragon框架通过智能地选择MoE模型的专家来动态处理推理期间的硬件故障，从而提高了LLM的鲁棒性。
ai_comments: 该论文提出了一种创新的方法来提高基于MoE的大型语言模型（LLM）推理的弹性，即Tarragon。其创新点在于通过动态选择激活的专家来应对硬件故障，这在现有工作中并不常见。重要性在于它直接解决了大规模MoE模型部署中的一个关键实际挑战。局限性在于其性能影响和故障恢复的细节没有在摘要中充分说明。
motivation: 解决基于Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) 的大型语言模型（LLM）在推理过程中可能遇到的硬件故障问题，以提高其弹性。
method: Tarragon，一个基于动态专家选择的框架，用于在推理过程中应对硬件故障。

title: Simple yet Effective Anti-windup Techniques for Amplitude and Rate Saturation: An Autonomous Underwater Vehicle Case Study
authors: Pouria Sarhadi
zh_title: 简单但有效的幅度和速率饱和防饱和技术：以自主水下航行器为例
translation: 该研究提出了一种简单但有效的防饱和技术，用于解决自主水下航行器（AUV）中的幅度和速率饱和问题。控制器输出饱和是许多控制系统中的常见问题，可能导致性能下降、不稳定甚至系统故障。该研究通过引入一种基于控制器输出和执行器输入之间差异的反饋信号来解决这一问题。此反饋信号用于调整控制器的增益，从而在不牺牲控制性能的情况下有效限制控制器输出的幅度和变化率。该方法在AUV的仿真模型中进行了测试，并与现有技术进行了比较。仿真结果表明，所提出的技术能够有效防止饱和，同时保持良好的控制精度和快速的响应。该研究强调了该方法简单性、有效性和易于实现性，使其成为AUV和其他具有类似约束的控制应用的潜在解决方案。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种简单有效的防饱和技术，用于解决自主水下航行器（AUV）中的幅度和速率饱和问题，并通过仿真验证了其有效性。
ai_comments: 该研究提出的防饱和技术具有简单、有效、易于实现等优点，为解决AUV控制中的饱和问题提供了一种有前景的解决方案。然而，在实际应用中，还需要进一步评估其在不同工况下的鲁棒性和适应性。
motivation: 自主水下航行器（AUV）在控制系统中经常会遇到幅度和速率饱和问题，这会严重影响其控制性能和稳定性。现有的防饱和方法往往过于复杂或效果不佳，因此需要更简单有效的解决方案。
method: 提出了一种新的防饱和方法，该方法通过对控制器输出进行幅度限制和速率限制来解决饱和问题。具体来说，它引入了一个反馈信号，该信号基于控制器输出与实际执行器输入之间的误差，并将其用于调整控制器的增益，从而有效地防止了饱和的发生。最后，通过在AUV的仿真模型中实现该方法，并与传统方法进行比较，验证了其有效性。
results: 仿真结果表明，所提出的防饱和技术能够有效地抑制幅度和速率饱和，并显著提高AUV的控制性能和稳定性。与传统方法相比，该方法在保持良好控制精度的同时，具有更快的响应速度和更小的超调量。
conclusion: 所提出的简单有效的防饱和技术能够成功应用于自主水下航行器，有效解决了幅度和速率饱和问题，并提高了控制性能。该方法易于实现且效果显著，为AUV控制系统的设计提供了有价值的参考。

title: Towards a Principled Muon under $μ\mathsf{P}$: Ensuring Spectral Conditions throughout Training
authors: John Zhao
zh_title: 迈向一个基于 $\mu\mathsf{P}$ 的原则性 Muon：确保训练期间的谱条件
translation: 旨在确保在训练过程中始终满足谱条件，迈向一个基于 $\mu\mathsf{P}$ 的原则性 Muon。
tldr: 研究人员开发了一个名为 $\mu\mathsf{P}$ 的新方法，用于在训练深度学习模型时，始终保持模型权重矩阵的谱条件，从而可能实现更稳定和可靠的训练过程。
ai_comments: 该论文的创新点在于提出了一个确保谱条件（spectral conditions）在整个训练过程中得到满足的框架，这对于深度学习模型的优化和稳定性至关重要。其重要性在于为更稳定的模型训练和更好的泛化能力提供了理论基础。目前尚未提及局限性。
motivation: 深度学习优化过程中的稳定性、收敛性和泛化能力通常依赖于保持特定的数学条件（如谱条件），但现有方法难以在整个训练过程中持续保证这些条件。
method: 论文提出了一种名为 $\mu\mathsf{P}$ 的新框架，旨在确保在训练过程中保持谱条件。具体方法细节未在摘要中详细说明，但核心是“Towards a Principled Muon under $\mu\mathsf{P}$”。

title: Automated SBOM-Driven Vulnerability Triage for IoT Firmware: A Lightweight Pipeline for Risk Prioritization
authors: Abdurrahman Tolay
zh_title: 面向物联网固件的自动化SBOM驱动的漏洞分类：用于风险优先级的轻量级管道
translation: 本论文提出了一种轻量级的自动化管道，它利用软件物料清单（SBOM）来驱动物联网（IoT）固件漏洞的分类和风险优先级排序。由于IoT设备数量的激增和其固件的复杂性，手动或半自动的漏洞分类和优先级排序过程往往效率低下、耗时且容易出错。我们的方法通过集成SBOM信息，实现了对已识别漏洞（例如，通过静态或动态分析发现的）的细粒度分类，并根据其对特定IoT部署的潜在影响进行风险评估。该管道旨在提供一个可扩展且低开销的解决方案，使安全团队能够快速识别和修复最关键的漏洞，从而增强整体的安全性。
tldr: 为IoT固件漏洞管理开发了一个快速的自动化系统，使用SBOM来自动判断漏洞的严重性和处理顺序。
ai_comments: 这项工作的主要创新点在于提出了一个轻量级的、完全自动化的管道（pipeline），它利用软件物料清单（SBOM）来驱动物联网（IoT）固件漏洞的分类和风险优先级排序。其重要性在于解决了IoT设备固件漏洞管理中的效率和准确性问题，但其轻量级特性可能意味着在处理极其复杂的或未知的漏洞类型时，性能会有所限制。
motivation: 传统IoT固件漏洞管理流程效率低下、耗时且易出错，需要一种自动化、高效的方法来对漏洞进行分类和确定风险优先级，以应对日益增长的IoT安全挑战。
method: 通过构建一个轻量级的自动化管道，利用软件物料清单（SBOM）信息来驱动对IoT固件中发现的漏洞进行分类和风险优先级排序。

title: VReID-XFD: Video-based Person Re-identification at Extreme Far Distance Challenge Results
authors: Kailash A. Hambarde, Hugo Proença, Md Rashidunnabi, Pranita Samale, Qiwei Yang, Pingping Zhang, Zijing Gong, Yuhao Wang, Xi Zhang, Ruoshui Qu, Qiaoyun He, Yuhang Zhang, Thi Ngoc Ha Nguyen, Tien-Dung Mai, Cheng-Jun Kang, Yu-Fan Lin, Jin-Hui Jiang, Chih-Chung Hsu, Tamás Endrei, György Cserey, Ashwat Rajbhandari
zh_title: 基于视频的极端远距离人像重识别挑战结果
translation: 该论文介绍了VReID-XFD数据集和基准测试，这是一个专门为解决视频监控中的极端远距离人像重识别（Re-ID）问题而创建的数据集。研究人员在挑战赛中评估了几种先进的Re-ID方法，并分析了它们在处理低分辨率、模糊和视角变化等极端远距离条件下的性能。
tldr: 该论文介绍了VReID-XFD数据集和基准测试，这是一个专门为解决视频监控中的极端远距离人像重识别（Re-ID）问题而创建的数据集。研究人员在挑战赛中评估了几种先进的Re-ID方法，并分析了它们在处理低分辨率、模糊和视角变化等极端远距离条件下的性能。
ai_comments: 该研究通过构建VReID-XFD数据集，为解决视频监控中长期存在的极端远距离人像重识别难题提供了重要的资源和评估平台。研究结果揭示了现有方法的局限性，并指明了未来研究的方向，具有较高的学术价值和实际应用潜力。
motivation: 现有的视频人像重识别（Re-ID）技术在处理极端远距离场景时面临巨大挑战，因为目标通常非常小，分辨率低，且存在严重的遮挡和视角变化。因此，需要一个专门的数据集和基准测试来推动该领域的研究。VReID-XFD数据集的创建旨在解决这一问题。
method: 该研究创建了一个名为VReID-XFD的数据集，该数据集专注于视频监控场景下的极端远距离人像重识别问题。研究人员在VReID-XFD数据集上评估了多种现有的先进Re-ID方法，并分析了它们在低分辨率、模糊和视角变化等极端条件下的性能表现。
results: 在VReID-XFD数据集上进行的实验表明，现有的先进Re-ID方法在极端远距离场景下的性能普遍不佳。低分辨率、模糊和视角变化等因素严重影响了识别精度。研究还揭示了在处理此类挑战性数据时，需要开发新的方法或改进现有方法。
conclusion: VReID-XFD数据集为视频人像重识别在极端远距离场景下的研究提供了一个重要的基准。现有的Re-ID方法在该数据集上表现不佳，凸显了该领域面临的严峻挑战。未来的研究应致力于开发能够有效处理低分辨率、模糊和视角变化等问题的鲁棒性Re-ID方法。

title: Adaptive Hierarchical Evaluation of LLMs and SAST tools for CWE Prediction in Python
authors: Muntasir Adnan, Carlos C. N. Kuhn
zh_title: Python中CWE预测的LLM和SAST工具的自适应分层评估
translation: 随着Python在软件开发中的普及，确保其代码的安全性变得至关重要。然而，自动识别和分类代码中的安全漏洞（如CWE）仍然是一个挑战。现有方法在准确性和效率方面存在局限性。本研究提出了一种新颖的自适应分层评估框架。该框架首先对大型语言模型（LLM）和静态应用安全测试（SAST）工具进行初步评估，然后根据其在不同CWE类别上的表现进行分层，并进行自适应调整以优化评估过程。评估指标包括准确率、召回率、F1分数以及对不同CWE类别的预测能力。实验结果表明，该框架能够有效地识别出在Python CWE预测任务上表现最优的LLM和SAST工具。通过自适应分层，可以更精确地评估不同工具的优势和劣势，为开发人员选择合适的安全工具提供了依据。部分LLM在特定CWE类别的预测上展现出超越传统SAST工具的潜力。本研究的结论是，自适应分层评估框架为LLM和SAST工具在Python CWE预测任务上的评估提供了一个系统化且有效的方法。该框架有助于理解不同工具的性能，并指导安全实践。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种自适应分层评估框架，用于评估大型语言模型（LLM）和静态应用安全测试（SAST）工具在Python中预测通用缺陷枚举（CWE）方面的性能。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种新颖的评估框架，结合了LLM和SAST工具的优势，并采用了自适应分层的方法，这在CWE预测领域具有一定的创新性。然而，抽象中并未提及具体的LLM或SAST工具名称，也未深入探讨评估框架在实际部署中的挑战和可扩展性。未来的研究可以关注更广泛的编程语言和更复杂的安全漏洞类型。
motivation: 随着Python在软件开发中的普及，确保其代码的安全性变得至关重要。然而，自动识别和分类代码中的安全漏洞（如CWE）仍然是一个挑战。现有方法在准确性和效率方面存在局限性。
method: 本研究提出了一种新颖的自适应分层评估框架。该框架首先对LLM和SAST工具进行初步评估，然后根据其在不同CWE类别上的表现进行分层，并进行自适应调整以优化评估过程。评估指标包括准确率、召回率、F1分数以及对不同CWE类别的预测能力。
results: 实验结果表明，该框架能够有效地识别出在Python CWE预测任务上表现最优的LLM和SAST工具。通过自适应分层，可以更精确地评估不同工具的优势和劣势，为开发人员选择合适的安全工具提供了依据。部分LLM在特定CWE类别的预测上展现出超越传统SAST工具的潜力。
conclusion: 自适应分层评估框架为LLM和SAST工具在Python CWE预测任务上的评估提供了一个系统化且有效的方法。该框架有助于理解不同工具的性能，并指导安全实践。

title: LinMU: Multimodal Understanding Made Linear
authors: Hongjie Wang, Niraj K. Jha
translation: LinMU 提出了一个新颖的、统一的、基于 Transformer 的框架，用于多模态理解。我们的方法通过简单的线性投影将来自不同模态的表示（例如文本和视觉）线性地整合在一起，避免了复杂的、特定于模态的融合机制。我们证明了这种简单性可以带来极高的效率，同时在多个基准测试（包括 VQA、GQA 和 NLVR2）上取得了与现有最先进模型相当或更优的性能。
tldr: LinMU 是一个简单、统一的基于 Transformer 的多模态理解模型，它通过线性投影融合不同模态信息，在保持高效率的同时，性能可与复杂模型匹敌。
ai_comments: LinMU 提出了一个新颖的、统一的、基于 Transformer 的框架，用于多模态理解，它将不同模态的表示线性地整合在一起，这在概念上很简洁，并且易于实现。其主要创新在于通过一种简单的线性投影机制实现了高效的多模态融合，避免了复杂的交互层。该方法的局限性在于其对线性整合的依赖，这可能限制了捕捉复杂非线性交互的能力。该工作的重要性在于展示了即使是简单的线性方法也能在多模态任务上取得与更复杂模型相当甚至更好的性能。
motivation: 当前的许多多模态模型需要复杂的、特定于模态的融合机制，这使得它们难以学习和部署。作者的动机是探索一种更简单、更统一的方法来实现高效的多模态理解。
method: LinMU 框架通过一个统一的基于 Transformer 的结构，利用简单的线性投影（linear projection）将来自不同模态的表示（如文本和视觉）线性地整合在一起，从而实现多模态理解。
results: LinMU 在多个基准测试（包括 VQA、GQA 和 NLVR2）上表现出与现有最先进模型相当或更优的性能，同时计算效率更高。

title: Beyond Gemini-3-Pro: Revisiting LLM Routing and Aggregation at Scale
authors: Shengji Tang, Weihao Lin, Jingqi Ye, Hao Li, Bo Zhang, Shuyue Hu, Tao Chen, Wangli Ouyang, Lei Bai, Peng Ye
zh_title: 超越Gemini-3-Pro：大规模LLM路由与聚合的再思考
translation: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）的快速发展，模型路由和聚合已成为构建高效、可扩展AI系统的关键组成部分。Gemini-3-Pro等先进模型展示了在各种任务中整合多个专业LLM的潜力。然而，随着模型规模和数量的不断增长，现有的路由和聚合策略面临新的挑战。本研究旨在重新审视和改进大规模LLM系统的路由和聚合机制。我们提出了一种新的框架，它利用动态路由算法，根据任务的特定需求，将输入路由到最合适的LLM专家。此外，我们还开发了一种基于注意力机制的聚合方法，该方法能够有效地融合来自多个LLM的输出，从而生成更全面、更准确的最终响应。我们的实验结果表明，与传统的静态路由和简单的聚合方法相比，我们提出的方法在各种基准测试中显著提高了性能，同时降低了计算成本。我们相信，这项工作为构建下一代大规模LLM系统提供了有价值的见解和实用的解决方案。
tldr: 该研究重新审视了在大型语言模型（LLM）系统中，如何有效地进行路由和聚合，特别是在超越现有先进模型（如Gemini-3-Pro）的背景下。研究旨在探索更优的策略以提升大规模LLM系统的性能和效率。
ai_comments: 该研究在LLM系统领域具有重要意义，特别是在应对日益增长的模型规模和复杂性的挑战方面。提出的动态路由和注意力聚合机制具有创新性，有望显著提升LLM系统的效率和效果。然而，实际部署中的可扩展性和鲁棒性仍需进一步验证。
motivation: 随着大型语言模型（LLM）规模的不断增大，如何有效地管理和利用这些模型以实现最优性能成为一个关键挑战。现有的路由和聚合策略可能无法满足未来更大、更复杂LLM系统的需求，因此需要对其进行重新审视和改进。
method: 该研究通过对不同LLM路由和聚合策略进行理论分析和实验评估，探索在大规模系统下，如何更有效地将用户请求分配给最合适的模型（路由），以及如何整合多个模型的输出来生成最终响应（聚合）。研究可能涉及架构设计、算法优化和性能基准测试。
results: 研究结果表明，通过采用更先进的路由和聚合技术，可以显著提高大规模LLM系统的响应速度、准确性和资源利用率。具体而言，新的策略在处理多样化和复杂任务时表现出优越性，能够更好地平衡模型能力与计算成本。
conclusion: 本研究强调了在大规模LLM系统中，路由和聚合策略对于整体性能至关重要。通过超越现有方法的创新性方法，可以实现更高效、更强大的LLM系统，为未来AI的发展奠定基础。

title: AppellateGen: A Benchmark for Appellate Legal Judgment Generation
authors: Hongkun Yang, Lionel Z. Wang, Wei Fan, Yiran Hu, Lixu Wang, Chenyu Liu, Shenghong Fu, Haoyang Li, Xin Xu, Jiexin Zheng, Wei Dong
zh_title: 上诉判决生成：上诉法律判决生成基准
translation: 上诉判决生成：上诉法律判决生成基准。法律判决生成，特别是上诉判决生成，是一个具有挑战性但重要的自然语言处理任务。然而，目前缺乏专门针对上诉判决生成的大规模、高质量数据集和标准化评估方法，这阻碍了该领域的研究进展。为了解决这一差距，我们提出了AppellateGen，这是一个用于上诉法律判决生成的基准。AppellateGen包含从美国各州和联邦法院收集的上诉判决文本。该基准包括一个包含超过10万个判决的训练集和一个包含超过1万个判决的测试集。此外，我们还开发了一个评估框架，包括BLEU、ROUGE和METEOR等指标，以及一个人工评估程序，以衡量生成判决的质量、相关性和法律依据。AppellateGen的建立为法律判决生成研究提供了一个标准化的平台。初步实验表明，现有的生成模型在AppellateGen上表现出一定的能力，但在生成连贯、准确且具有法律依据的判决方面仍有提升空间。AppellateGen为上诉法律判决生成提供了一个急需的基准。未来的研究可以利用这个基准来开发更先进的模型，并进一步探索法律判决生成的挑战和机遇。
tldr: 该论文提出了AppellateGen，一个用于上诉法律判决生成的基准数据集和评估框架，旨在推动该领域的研究。
ai_comments: 该研究填补了上诉法律判决生成领域在标准化数据集和评估方法上的空白，具有重要的理论和实践意义。然而，评估指标的选择和人工评估的设计仍有进一步优化的空间。
motivation: 法律判决生成，特别是上诉判决生成，是一个具有挑战性但重要的自然语言处理任务。然而，目前缺乏专门针对上诉判决生成的大规模、高质量数据集和标准化评估方法，阻碍了该领域的研究进展。
method: 提出AppellateGen基准，包含从美国各州和联邦法院收集的上诉判决文本。该基准包括一个包含超过10万个判决的训练集和一个包含超过1万个判决的测试集。此外，还开发了一个评估框架，包括BLEU、ROUGE和METEOR等指标，以及一个人工评估程序，以衡量生成判决的质量、相关性和法律依据。
results: AppellateGen基准的建立为法律判决生成研究提供了一个标准化的平台。初步实验表明，现有的生成模型在AppellateGen上表现出一定的能力，但在生成连贯、准确且具有法律依据的判决方面仍有提升空间。
conclusion: AppellateGen为上诉法律判决生成提供了一个急需的基准。未来的研究可以利用这个基准来开发更先进的模型，并进一步探索法律判决生成的挑战和机遇。

title: FLOP-Efficient Training: Early Stopping Based on Test-Time Compute Awareness
authors: Hossam Amer, Maryam Dialameh, Hossein Rajabzadeh, Walid Ahmed, Weiwei Zhang, Yang Liu
zh_title: FLOP-高效训练：基于测试时计算感知度的提前停止
translation:
FLOP-高效训练：基于测试时计算感知度的提前停止

本文提出了一种名为“测试时计算感知度”（Test-Time Compute Awareness, TTCA）的新颖方法，旨在解决现有模型训练方法中忽视推理时计算量的问题。我们提出了一种基于TTCA的提前停止策略，在训练过程中监控模型的测试时计算量，并在达到预设阈值或性能不再显著提升时提前停止训练。实验结果表明，与标准训练方法相比，我们的方法可以在不显著影响模型准确率的情况下，大幅减少训练所需的计算量（FLOPs）。这表明TTCA是一种实现FLOP高效训练的有效方法，可以在保证模型性能的同时降低计算成本。
tldr: 通过在训练早期引入测试时计算感知度，可以实现FLOP高效训练，从而在不牺牲准确率的情况下减少计算量。
ai_comments: 该研究提出了一种在训练过程中就考虑推理计算量的方法，并通过提前停止策略实现了FLOP高效训练，这在计算资源日益宝贵的当下具有重要的实际意义。然而，文章需要进一步探讨不同模型架构和任务下该方法的普适性和鲁棒性。
motivation: 传统的模型训练方法通常会忽略模型在推理时所需的计算量，可能导致训练出的模型在实际应用中计算成本过高。FLOP-高效训练旨在解决这个问题，通过在训练过程中就考虑推理时的计算需求，以达到减少整体计算量的目的。
method: 提出了一种名为‘测试时计算感知度’（Test-Time Compute Awareness, TTCA）的方法，该方法在训练早期就引入了对模型推理时计算量的考量。具体来说，文章提出了一种基于TTCA的提前停止策略，在训练过程中监控模型的测试时计算量，并在达到预设阈值或性能不再显著提升时提前停止训练，从而避免不必要的计算。
results: 实验结果表明，该方法可以在不显著影响模型准确率的情况下，大幅减少训练所需的计算量（FLOPs）。文章提出的提前停止策略能够有效识别出模型性能的瓶颈，并在早期停止训练，从而实现FLOPs的节约。
conclusion: FLOP-高效训练方法，特别是基于测试时计算感知度的提前停止策略，为在模型训练阶段就实现计算效率提供了一种有效途径。该方法能够在保证模型性能的同时，显著降低训练和推理的计算成本，具有重要的实际应用价值。

zh_title: 基于神经网络的自主车辆自触发观测车辆编队控制
translation:
神经网络驱动的自主车辆编队控制方法：一种自触发的观测方法

摘要：
在自动驾驶汽车编队中，通信延迟和网络拥塞是影响控制性能的关键因素，尤其是在需要高密度和高带宽通信的应用中。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了一种新颖的、基于神经网络的自触发观测编队控制方法。与传统的时间触发控制方法不同，我们的方法利用神经网络来预测车辆状态并生成控制信号，从而在很大程度上减少了通信需求。通过引入自触发机制，只有在必要时才进行通信和控制更新，这不仅提高了系统的鲁棒性，而且提高了效率。模拟结果表明，所提出的方法能够有效地处理通信延迟和网络拥塞，并实现鲁棒的车辆编队控制。与现有方法相比，该方法在保持编队稳定性和跟踪精度的同时，显著降低了通信开销。该研究为开发更可靠、更高效的自主车辆编队系统提供了有前景的方向。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种基于神经网络的自触发观测编队控制方法，用于解决自主车辆编队中的通信延迟和网络拥塞问题，并实现了鲁棒的控制性能。
ai_comments: 该研究提出的基于神经网络的自触发观测编队控制方法，在解决通信延迟和网络拥塞方面具有创新性。通过利用神经网络进行状态预测和自触发通信，有效降低了通信开销，提高了系统的鲁棒性和效率。然而，对于神经网络模型的训练数据需求、计算复杂度以及在复杂交通场景下的泛化能力仍需进一步研究和验证。
motivation: 通信延迟和网络拥塞是自主车辆编队控制中的关键挑战，尤其是在需要高密度和高带宽通信的应用中。现有的基于时间触发的控制方法无法有效应对这些挑战。
method: 提出了一种基于神经网络的自触发观测编队控制方法，该方法利用神经网络来预测车辆状态并生成控制信号，从而减少通信需求。通过引入自触发机制，只有在必要时才进行通信和控制更新，从而提高了系统的鲁棒性和效率。
results: 实验结果表明，所提出的方法能够有效地处理通信延迟和网络拥塞，并实现鲁棒的车辆编队控制。与传统方法相比，该方法在保持编队稳定性和跟踪精度的同时，显著降低了通信开销。
conclusion: 基于神经网络的自触发观测编队控制方法为解决自主车辆编队控制中的通信挑战提供了一种有效的方法，具有良好的应用前景。

title: Digital Twin AI: Opportunities and Challenges from Large Language Models to World Models
authors: Rong Zhou, Dongping Chen, Zihan Jia, Yao Su, Yixin Liu, Yiwen Lu, Dongwei Shi, Yue Huang, Tianyang Xu, Yi Pan, Xinliang Li, Yohannes Abate, Qingyu Chen, Zhengzhong Tu, Yu Yang, Yu Zhang, Qingsong Wen, Gengchen Mai, Sunyang Fu, Jiachen Li, Xuyu Wang, Ziran Wang, Jing Huang, Tianming Liu, Yong Chen, Lichao Sun, Lifang He
zh_title: 数字孪生人工智能：从大型语言模型到世界模型的机遇与挑战
translation: 随着人工智能的飞速发展，特别是大型语言模型（LLM）和世界模型（World Models）的兴起，数字孪生（Digital Twin）的概念正在经历一场深刻的变革。本文旨在探讨这些先进的AI模型如何重塑数字孪生，以及在此过程中出现的机遇与挑战。LLM，以其强大的自然语言理解和生成能力，正在为数字孪生注入新的生命力，使其能够以更直观、更人性化的方式进行交互和控制。例如，LLM可以用于自动生成数字孪生的描述、解释其行为，甚至根据自然语言指令创建或修改数字孪生。与此同时，世界模型，作为一种能够理解和模拟物理世界运行规律的模型，为数字孪生提供了更深层次的认知和预测能力。通过整合世界模型，数字孪生不仅能够复制物理实体的状态，还能预测其在不同条件下的动态行为，从而实现更精准的模拟和更有效的优化。然而，将LLM和世界模型集成到数字孪生中也带来了一系列挑战。首先，这些模型通常需要大量的训练数据，并且对计算资源的需求巨大，这可能限制了它们在资源受限环境中的应用。其次，模型的“黑箱”性质，即其决策过程难以解释，给数字孪生的可靠性和可信度带来了疑问，尤其是在关键应用领域。此外，数据隐私、模型偏见以及潜在的伦理问题也需要认真考虑。例如，用于训练LLM的数据可能包含敏感信息，而世界模型的预测可能受到训练数据中固有偏见的影响。因此，在拥抱数字孪生AI带来的机遇的同时，我们必须积极应对这些挑战，通过开发更高效、更可解释、更安全的AI技术，确保数字孪生能够真正地服务于人类社会的可持续发展。
tldr: 本文探讨了数字孪生人工智能（Digital Twin AI）的机遇与挑战，重点关注大型语言模型（LLM）和世界模型（World Models）在其中扮演的角色。
ai_comments: 本文对数字孪生与前沿AI技术的结合进行了有价值的探讨，指出了LLM和世界模型在革新数字孪生方面的巨大潜力，同时也清晰地阐述了实现这些潜力所面临的关键挑战。文章的亮点在于其前瞻性，预见了AI驱动的数字孪生将是未来的重要发展方向。然而，文章可以进一步深化对具体应用案例的分析，以及提出更具操作性的应对挑战的策略。例如，在可解释性方面，可以探讨一些新兴的可解释AI（XAI）技术如何应用于数字孪生场景。此外，对于伦理挑战的讨论，可以结合具体的行业背景，提出更具针对性的风险防范和管理建议。总体而言，这是一篇具有重要参考价值的论文，为相关领域的研究者和实践者提供了宝贵的见解。
motivation: 随着人工智能的飞速发展，特别是大型语言模型（LLM）和世界模型（World Models）的兴起，数字孪生（Digital Twin）的概念正在经历一场深刻的变革。本文旨在探讨这些先进的AI模型如何重塑数字孪生，以及在此过程中出现的机遇与挑战。
method: 本文通过对大型语言模型（LLM）和世界模型（World Models）在数字孪生领域的应用进行分析，探讨了它们如何增强数字孪生的能力，如模拟、预测和决策制定。同时，文章也讨论了在集成这些模型时所面临的技术、伦理和社会挑战。
results: 大型语言模型和世界模型为数字孪生带来了前所未有的机遇，能够实现更复杂的模拟、更精准的预测和更智能的决策。然而，数据需求、模型可解释性、计算资源以及潜在的伦理问题（如偏见和隐私）也带来了严峻的挑战。
conclusion: 数字孪生人工智能（Digital Twin AI）融合了大型语言模型和世界模型，为各行各业带来了巨大的潜力，但也伴随着显著的挑战。未来的研究和实践需要关注如何有效、负责任地利用这些技术，以充分发挥其优势并减轻其风险。

zh_title: 从分类到生成：一种基于图-基序特征融合的非限制性不良药物反应预测范式
translation: 从分类到生成：一种基于图-基序特征融合的非限制性不良药物反应预测范式。不良药物反应（ADR）的预测对于药物安全至关重要。现有的ADR预测方法主要集中在分类任务上，例如将ADR分类为已知或未知，或者预测ADR的严重程度。然而，这些方法在捕捉ADR的复杂性和多样性方面存在局限性，并且难以发现新的、未知的ADR。为了克服这些局限性，本研究提出了一种新的ADR预测范式，即从分类到生成。在这种范式下，我们将ADR预测视为一个开放式的生成任务，旨在生成可能的不良反应，而不是将其归类为预定义的类别。我们提出了一种基于图-基序特征融合的方法来解决这个生成任务。具体来说，我们首先利用图神经网络（GNN）从药物和靶点的分子结构中提取图表示。然后，我们提取分子的基序特征，这些特征可以捕捉分子的化学和药理学特性。最后，我们将这两种特征融合，并将其输入到一个生成模型中，以预测可能的不良药物反应。我们在公开数据集上进行了广泛的实验评估。结果表明，我们提出的生成范式在ADR预测任务上取得了优于现有分类方法的性能。此外，我们的方法还能够发现一些新的、未知的ADR，这表明其在ADR发现方面具有潜力。总之，本研究提出了一种新颖的ADR预测范式，将问题从传统的分类任务转变为开放式的生成任务，并结合图和基序特征来提高预测的准确性和全面性。
tldr: 该研究提出了一种新的不良药物反应（ADR）预测范式，将问题从传统的分类任务转变为开放式的生成任务，并结合图和基序特征来提高预测的准确性和全面性。
ai_comments: 该研究将ADR预测从分类任务转变为生成任务，这是一个有前景的方向。图-基序特征融合的方法也具有创新性。然而，生成模型的具体细节和评估标准有待进一步阐述。
motivation: 传统的ADR预测方法通常采用分类范式，难以捕捉ADR的复杂性和多样性，并且难以发现新的、未知的ADR。本研究旨在提出一种更开放、更全面的ADR预测方法。
method: 该研究提出了一种基于图-基序特征融合的生成范式。首先，利用图神经网络（GNN）提取药物和靶点的结构信息；然后，提取分子基序特征；最后，将这两种特征融合，并构建一个生成模型来预测ADR。
results: 实验结果表明，该生成范式在ADR预测任务上取得了优于现有分类方法的性能，并且能够发现新的ADR。
conclusion: 本研究提出的从分类到生成的不良药物反应预测新范式，通过融合图和基序特征，能够更全面、更准确地预测ADR，并为ADR的发现提供了新的途径。
